title: Appending a program preserves a call bound
statement: Let $P$ and $P'$ be programs, let $p,d,T$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a finite list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a memory function, and let $R$ be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. If program $p$ in $P$, called on inputs $\mathrm{vals}$ with initial memory $\mu$ and depth parameter $d$, can execute within cost $T$ and produce an output and final memory satisfying $R$, then the same call in the concatenated program $P$ followed by $P'$ can do so as well.
hypotheses_covered: A program $P$ and an appended program $P'$
Natural-number procedure index $p$, depth parameter $d$, and cost bound $T$
